rem:mass-tower-syt-cells:
Remark SYT / Jucys–Murphy reindexing of the mass tower pair set. This remark reframes the pair blow-up set \mathcal{P}_n (jet-brane reformulation) using the Jucys--Murphy (JM) elements and standard Young tableaux (SYT). The motivation: empirical probes show the optimal \mathcal{P}_n is all pairs with no distance restriction ([descent rate categorical](#sim:descent-rate-canonical evaluation)), which is most accordingly expressed in the JM / SYT cell basis.

Jucys--Murphy elements

For H_n(R, q) with generators \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1}, the Jucys--Murphy (JM) elements are

  L_k = \sigma_{k-1} \sigma_{k-2} \cdots \sigma_1 \sigma_1 \cdots \sigma_{k-1},
  \qquad k = 1, \ldots, n,

with L_1 = 1. They commute pairwise ([L_i, L_j] = 0) and act diagonally on the Young basis: for a SYT T of shape \lambda and basis vector v_T,

  L_k \, v_T
  = q^{2 c_T(k)} \, v_T,

where c_T(k) = j - i is the content of the cell of T containing the integer k (cell at row i, column j).

SYT cell reindexing

The pair set \mathcal{P}_n in jet-brane form is accordingly cell-indexed via JM:

  \mathcal{P}_n
  \;\longleftrightarrow\;
  \{\{k_1, k_2\} \subseteq \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}\},

with each pair \{k_1, k_2\} corresponding to a pair of cells in any SYT shape \lambda \vdash n. Under this reindexing:

  • Generator distance |i - j| is not preserved — JM indices k range over cells, not over generator positions, so there is no "adjacent vs far-commuting" distinction.

  • Eigenvalue product is diagonal: on v_T,

   L_{k_1} L_{k_2} \, v_T
   = q^{2(c_T(k_1) + c_T(k_2))} \, v_T.
  • All pairs are on equal footing: [L_i, L_j] = 0 by construction. This matches the empirical finding that \beta(d) = 1 uniformly across distances ([descent rate canonical evaluation](#sim:descent-rate-canonical evaluation)).

Reformulated mass tower

Using JM / SYT cells, the per-jet-level contribution becomes:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:syt-cell-tower}
  \mathfrak{m}^{(n)}(\varrho)
  =
  \bigl\lvert\textstyle\prod_{k=1}^{n} \hat V_k^{\mathrm{JM}}\bigr\rvert
  + \textstyle\sum_{k=1}^n \Phi_q(|\hat V_k^{\mathrm{JM}}|)
  + z^2 \textstyle\sum_{1 \leq k_1 < k_2 \leq n}
      \Phi_q(|\hat V_{k_1}^{\mathrm{JM}} \hat V_{k_2}^{\mathrm{JM}}|),
\end{equation}

where \hat V_k^{\mathrm{JM}} is the Markov-trace-weighted eigenvalue of L_k in the braid word's irrep, weighted by the Plancherel measure on \lambda \vdash n:

  \hat V_k^{\mathrm{JM}}
  =
  \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} w_\lambda
    \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)}
      \mu_T \cdot q^{2 c_T(k)},

with \mu_T = normalised SYT Plancherel weight.

The pair weight z^2 in the cross sum matches the generator-indexed form of the mass-endomorphism tower and is justified universally (all k_1 < k_2, not just adjacent pairs) by the Markov-trace factorization theorem: two successive Markov peels of commuting elements each contribute a factor z, so \mathrm{tr}_M(L_{k_1} L_{k_2}) = z^2. In the JM / SYT reindexing this is automatic — [L_i, L_j] = 0 makes every pair structurally equivalent to the far-commuting case covered by the factorization theorem.

Advantages

  1. All pairs automatic. [L_i, L_j] = 0 gives a symmetric pair sum with no adjacent/far distinction — consistent with the empirical \beta(d) = 1.
  2. Descent structure visible. The descent involution acts on SYT shapes by box-removal: a jet-(n+1) transient supported on a shape \lambda \vdash n+1 descends to jet-n when the shape's removable corner is vacated. This is the formal descent that the generator-indexed form struggles to express.
  3. Multi-level sum structural. Summing over jet levels becomes summing over the SYT tree: each level adds one cell. The jet tower \{A_n\} is built by box additions; the mass tower sums contributions at each addition.

Implementation path

  1. Compute L_k seminormal eigenvalues q^{2 c_T(k)} per SYT (from the seminormal matrix representation).
  2. Build \hat V_k^{\mathrm{JM}} via Plancherel-weighted sum over SYTs.
  3. Sum cell-pair \Phi_q contributions (all \binom{n}{2} pairs, no distance filter).
  4. Iterate over jet levels n = 0, 1, \ldots, N and sum.

Empirical validation

Direct evaluation computes \hat V_k^{\mathrm{JM}} for k = 1, \ldots, 3A on the atom braid word and assembles the tower of the cell-tower equation. Against the scalar all-pairs form of the mass-endomorphism tower, with E_0 calibrated per path on the proton:

Atom scalar all-pairs JM all-pairs
D 0.120% 0.105%
T 18.0% 0.277%
3He 60.1% 0.219%

The scalar path suffers a pair-pathology on T and 3He even after mass-endomorphism-tower.md's all-pairs form is used; the JM path closes the residual by carrying the per-SYT content structure missing from a scalar factorization.

Open question

Does the SYT-cell form reproduce the generator-indexed form at each n, or only up to a descent involution? Naively the two should agree at the per-irrep level (change of basis within each V_\lambda), but the pair-count and independence-claim structure may differ, since JM pairs are always commuting and have no "adjacent vs far" ambiguity — a distinction now formally absorbed into the Markov-trace factorization theorem. The T/3He residual closure in the table above suggests the JM form is not only a basis change: it captures SYT-content correlations that the scalar factorization drops.
prose:intro-mutant-jones-bloch-group:
A classic limitation of the uncolored Jones polynomial—and hence of the bare closure Markov trace—is its inability to distinguish mutant knots such as the 11-crossing Conway and Kinoshita–Terasaka pair, which differ by a 180^\circ Conway-sphere involution. Mutation preserves the coloured Jones polynomials and the hyperbolic volume, so \mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{KT}) = \mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{Conway}) (Ruberman's theorem; see the Conway–Kinoshita–Terasaka volume test). The blindness of the trace is a theorem, not only an observation: invariants whose weight systems factor through intersection graphs, which include the Jones and HOMFLY polynomials, take equal values on mutant knots (Chmutov–Lando, arXiv:0704.1313, Thm. 3).

This section shows how the bi-filtered Hecke framework resolves mutant ambiguity. Whereas the level-zero closure trace collapses the four-strand Conway tangle to a symmetric scalar, the knot-indexed convolution grid and the non-commutative Wedderburn Fourier transform retain the off-diagonal representation matrix elements before closure. Pushing these representation invariants into the Bloch group B(\mathbb{C}) is proposed to separate the Conway and Kinoshita–Terasaka complements (not established; it cannot rest on volume, which the two share), links the Pieri photon shift and JSJ tower bridge to the WKB Green's function of the quantum dilogarithm, and identifies the Borromean complement's class in the Bloch group via Poincaré–Lefschetz duality.

The grid structure

Most knot-indexed operations operate algebraically at depth n=0 without polylogarithms. They shift the knot-index axis strictly through structural translation. The archimedean image emerges at higher depths only post-realization via \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}.

The bi-filtration separates input shape (depth-0 knot index) from output transcendence depth (post-realization polylogarithm). The interface coupling \bowtie_K exemplifies this as a strict depth-0 convolution in the Hecke algebra, manipulating elements algebraically without generating higher-order transcendental terms.

This grid systematizes existing convolutions, predicts compositions between depths, and identifies open falsifiability targets like high-n chiral entries.

conj:categorical-higgs-mechanism:
Conjecture Categorical Higgs mechanism: Goldstone-eating as topological linking. The symmetry-breaking Higgs mechanism SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \to U(1)_{\rm em} admits a categorical formulation. Goldstone boson consumption corresponds exactly to the topological linking of closed braids.

Pre-symmetry breaking, the four electroweak gauge bosons form individual 1-component knots. A Higgs doublet provides four real scalar degrees of freedom, also corresponding to 1-component knots.

Post-breaking, the vacuum expectation value induces topological linking. Three gauge bosons each fuse with a Goldstone boson, forming 2-component links. The linking number \mathrm{lk} = 1 encodes the broken-generator multiplicity. The remaining unbroken photon survives as a 1-component knot. The surviving Higgs scalar similarly remains an independent mediator.

The mass of each post-breaking boson evaluates as the Markov trace of its new 2-component link, weighted by the appropriate Hoefsmit projector. Categorical linking supplies the precise operation that differentiates massive force-links from massless matter-knots.
conj:categorical-linking-operation:
Conjecture Categorical linking operation \mathrm{Lk}_R: ribbon-category dual of topological linking number. Let \mathbf{C} be a rigid monoidal R-linear category with braiding c_{X, Y}, and let A be the Frobenius-Hopf aether. The categorical linking operation is the family of R-linear maps

  \mathrm{Lk}_R^{(k)}
  \;\colon\;
  \mathrm{Hom}_R(\mathbf{1}, A) \otimes_R \mathrm{Hom}_R(\mathbf{1}, A)
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathrm{End}_R(A),

defined by

  \mathrm{Lk}_R^{(k)}(a, b)
  \;:=\;
  (\mathrm{id}_A \otimes \tau_R) \,\circ\,
  \bigl( c_{A, A}^{\,k} \circ (a \otimes b) \otimes \mathrm{id}_A \bigr)
  \,\circ\, \mathrm{id}_A.

This evaluates the categorical trace-cut of a 2-component link: closing one component via the trace leaves the other as a free endomorphism.

Formal properties

  1. Linearity (proved): \mathrm{Lk}_R^{(k)} is R-bilinear.
  2. Reduction at k = 0 (proved): \mathrm{Lk}_R^{(0)}(a, b) = \tau_R(b) \cdot a^*, recovering the rank-1 dual endomorphism.
  3. Multiplicativity (proved): Additional linkings map to pre-composition with c_{A, A}.
  4. Trace-cut symmetry (conditional): Cutting the left component produces the \iota-conjugate operation \mathrm{Lk}_R^{(-k)}(b, a).
  5. Bar-involution compatibility (conditional): \iota(\mathrm{Lk}_R^{(k)}(a, b)) = \mathrm{Lk}_R^{(-k)}(\iota(a), \iota(b)).

Properties 1-3 hold generically in rigid monoidal categories. Properties 4-5 require specific ribbon trace structures.

Significance for electroweak symmetry breaking

The Higgs mechanism lifts a gauge boson from \mathrm{Hom}_R(\mathbf{1}, A) (unbroken 1-component knot) to \mathrm{End}_R(A) (broken 2-component link). The linking operation \mathrm{Lk}_R^{(1)} realizes this lift categorically. The post-EWSB boson mass is the resulting Markov trace evaluated on the broken endomorphism.
rem:categorical-linking-operation-interp: Remark Proof scope of Property 1: linearity is a generic categorical fact. The proofs for properties 1-3 utilize only standard rigid monoidal axioms. They apply generically across any suitable category supporting trace-cuts and require no QOU-specific Hecke algebra or Markov trace assumptions.

rem:conway-kt-vol-injectivity-test:
Remark Conway--Kinoshita--Terasaka mutant pair: a volume-injectivity check for the depth correspondence. The transcendental accounting framework predicts that identical Jones polynomials imply identical hyperbolic volumes. The Conway and Kinoshita-Terasaka mutant knots share exactly the same Jones polynomial and the same hyperbolic volume, satisfying this prediction.

Mutation preserves the colored Jones polynomials and the hyperbolic volume universally (Ruberman's theorem). The prediction therefore holds trivially for mutants.

For rigorous falsifiability, the Vol-injectivity hypothesis requires a non-mutant knot pair sharing identical Jones polynomials but exhibiting distinct hyperbolic volumes. No such pairs are currently known within the Bring-embeddable class. Discovering one would strictly falsify the J^{(2)} Vol-injectivity claim, though the higher-color asymptotic Volume Conjecture mechanism would remain mathematically consistent.
rem:jones-faithfulness-crossing-8:
Remark Bring-embeddable Jones-faithfulness: theorem at crossing \leq 10, falsified for Conway-KT at crossing 11. The Hoste-Thistlethwaite-Weeks enumeration proved that distinct prime knots up to 10 crossings possess unique Jones polynomials. The Conway-KT mutant pair breaks this uniqueness precisely at 11 crossings.

Since both the Conway and KT knots are Bring-embeddable (genus 3), Jones-faithfulness strictly fails for Bring-embeddable knots at crossing 11. However, Ruberman's theorem forces their volumes to match, maintaining the Vol-injectivity prediction. The open challenge remains locating non-mutant Jones-coincident pairs above 11 crossings to construct a definitive falsification target.

lem:degree-one-braid-trivial-volume:
Lemma Braid words of a degree-one element have non-hyperbolic closures. Statement. Let \gamma = c_0\,\mathbf{1} + \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \phi_i\, \sigma_i^{\epsilon_i}, with \epsilon_i \in \{\pm 1\}, be a degree-one element of H_n(q). Every braid word in the support of \gamma has a non-hyperbolic closure: \overline{\mathbf{1}} is the n-component unlink and \overline{\sigma_i^{\pm 1}} is the (n-1)-component unlink. Hence the hyperbolic volume vanishes word by word:

  \mathrm{Vol}\bigl(\overline{w}\bigr) \;=\; 0
  \qquad \text{for every word } w \in \{\mathbf{1}, \sigma_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, \sigma_{n-1}^{\pm 1}\}.

The volume is a function on braid words, not a linear map on H_n(q). No linear map on H_n(q) agrees with the hyperbolic volume on all braid words, so the statement does not extend to a volume of the element \gamma itself.

The same holds for a photon \gamma(\varphi) = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} \in H_3(q). Its support words are \mathbf{1}, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}. They close to the three-component unlink, the two-component unlink (twice) and the unknot. The vertex word \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} uses each generator once, so its closure is the unknot. Every support word of a photon therefore has volume 0. The degree-one element above is not a photon, because it has no vertex term. On one strand pair with all \epsilon_i = +1 and c_0 = 1 it is the photon's specialisation \varphi_{01} = 0.
prop:pieri-photon-shift:
Proposition Multiplication by a degree-one Hecke element is a non-commutative Fourier shift (Pieri rule). Statement. Let \lambda = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2) \vdash n be a partition with at most two rows (the shapes seen by \mathrm{SU}_q(2) on V_\square^{\otimes n}), and let \beta_m \in H_n(q) be supported purely on the \lambda-block. Let \gamma be a photon \gamma(\varphi) = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_a + \varphi_1\sigma_b + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_a\sigma_b^{-1} on consecutive generators a, b = a + 1 with b \leq n, so that at most one of its three strands lies beyond the n strands of \beta_m (its degree-one specialisation \varphi_{01} = 0 included).

  1. If b \leq n - 1, then \gamma\beta_m \in H_n(q) and \mathrm{supp}(\gamma\beta_m) \subseteq \{\lambda\}.
  2. If b = n, read \gamma\beta_m in H_{n+1}(q). Its Wedderburn support is contained in the set of \mu \vdash n + 1 with \mu \supset \lambda, namely \lambda + \square := (\lambda_1 + 1, \lambda_2), \lambda - \square := (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) (when it is a partition) and (\lambda_1, \lambda_2, 1). On V_\square^{\otimes(n+1)} the three-row component acts by zero, so there
  \mathrm{supp}\bigl(\gamma \cdot \beta_m\bigr)
  \;\subseteq\;
  \{\lambda + \square\} \;\cup\; \{\lambda - \square\}.

The name \lambda - \square comes from the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) reading: a complete two-box column is the trivial weight, so (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) has the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) highest weight of (\lambda_1 - 1, \lambda_2). As a partition it has one box more than \lambda, not one less.

The case a = n (two strands beyond \beta_m) is not covered: there the product lies in H_{n+2}(q) and the support can reach partitions with two more boxes.
prf:pieri-photon-shift:
Proof Proof of pieri photon shift. Let \gamma = \gamma(\varphi) be a photon. Its degree-one specialisation \varphi_{01} = 0 is the element of the degree-one volume lemma. Let \beta_m be supported purely on the \lambda-block. Here the support \mathrm{supp}(x) of an element is the set of labels in the Young lattice indexing the isotypic components on which x has a non-zero component, read through Schur–Weyl duality: at generic q, the Hecke algebra H_n(q) and \mathrm{SU}_q(2) generate each other's commutant on V_\square^{\otimes n}, where V_\square is the two-dimensional fundamental representation, and the simple module V_\lambda is matched with the \lambda-isotypic component of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) action [kassel1995]. The hypothesis on \beta_m says its image lies in the V_\lambda-isotypic component.

Step 1: reduction by linearity. Write \gamma\beta_m = \beta_m + \varphi_0\,\sigma_a\beta_m + \varphi_1\,\sigma_b\beta_m + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_a\sigma_b^{-1}\beta_m. Since \mathrm{supp}(x + y) \subseteq \mathrm{supp}(x) \cup \mathrm{supp}(y), it suffices to bound the support of each summand.

Case b \leq n - 1. Every term lies in H_n(q); the vertex term does too, because \sigma_b^{-1} = \sigma_b - h with h = q - q^{-1}. The central idempotent e_\lambda of H_n(q) commutes with every element, and \beta_m = e_\lambda \beta_m, so \gamma\beta_m = \gamma e_\lambda \beta_m = e_\lambda\gamma\beta_m. Hence \mathrm{supp}(\gamma\beta_m) \subseteq \{\lambda\}.

Case b = n. All four terms lie in H_{n+1}(q) \supset H_n(q). Let e_\mu, \mu \vdash n + 1, be the central idempotents of H_{n+1}(q). By the branching rule for H_n(q) \subset H_{n+1}(q) at generic q (the same as for S_n \subset S_{n+1}), e_\mu e_\lambda = 0 unless \mu \supset \lambda. For any x \in H_{n+1}(q),

  e_\mu\, x\, \beta_m \;=\; x\, e_\mu\, e_\lambda\, \beta_m ,

since e_\mu is central. So e_\mu \gamma \beta_m = 0 unless \mu \supset \lambda. The partitions \mu \vdash n + 1 with \mu \supset \lambda are (\lambda_1 + 1, \lambda_2), (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) when \lambda_2 < \lambda_1, and (\lambda_1, \lambda_2, 1). By Schur–Weyl duality for \mathrm{SU}_q(2) [kassel1995], H_{n+1}(q) acts on V_\square^{\otimes(n+1)} through its two-row quotient, so the three-row component acts by zero there. This gives the stated containment. \blacksquare

Scope. The proposition gives a containment of supports, not equality. The actual coefficients are dictated by the \phi_i and the Hecke-algebra 6j-symbols (matrix elements of the basis change between the seminormal basis and the inclusion basis); they are not computed here. For the purposes of the QOU mass-formula pipeline, only the support statement is used: it bounds the spectral spread induced by a single photon coupling to one box.

Relation to the volume vanishing. The degree-one volume lemma says every braid word in the support of \gamma has volume 0. The Pieri shift is the representation-theoretic counterpart: it tracks how \gamma moves the Wedderburn support without itself contributing to the archimedean volume of \overline{\gamma}.
rem:pieri-photon-shift-interpretation: Remark The Pieri box-shift as a non-commutative Fourier single-step shift. Under the non-commutative Fourier transform, multiplying by an element of the next Hecke algebra moves the Young-diagram support up the Young lattice by exactly one box, analogous to a single-step translation on the commutative frequency lattice. For two-row partitions, read as \mathrm{SU}_q(2) spins j = (\lambda_1 - \lambda_2)/2, the two possible added boxes raise or lower the spin by 1/2. In both cases a box is added; neither case removes one.
prf:degree-one-braid-trivial-volume:
Proof Proof of degree one braid trivial volume. The hyperbolic volume vanishes on every non-hyperbolic link, by convention (Kashaev--Murakami--Murakami convention).

  1. Identity. \overline{\mathbf{1}} is the n-component unlink, which is not hyperbolic, so \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{\mathbf{1}}) = 0.

  2. One crossing. \sigma_i^{\pm 1} joins strands i and i+1 by a single crossing; its closure is an unknot together with n-2 disjoint unknotted strands, an (n-1)-component unlink. It is not hyperbolic, so \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{\sigma_i^{\pm 1}}) = 0.

These are all the words in the support of \gamma. \blacksquare

Why the volume is not linear. The two cases above cannot be combined by extending \mathrm{Vol} to a linear functional on H_n(q), because no such linear extension exists. The six positive permutation braids \mathbf{1}, \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_1\sigma_2, \sigma_2\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 span H_3(q), and their closures (unlinks, the unknot, the Hopf link) all have volume 0. A linear map that agreed with \mathrm{Vol} on them would vanish on all of H_3(q), including on \sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1}\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1}, whose closure is 4_1 with \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2.0299\ldots \neq 0. The first half of this argument is proved: a linear map that vanishes on a set vanishes on its span.

Scope. The lemma establishes only the archimedean shadow — the real-valued volume image. It does not identify \gamma with the gauge boson of any physical theory; that identification is interpretive and is discussed in breit-wheeler-vertex and the photon-energy section of the manuscript.

Exclusion. Every braid word in the support of a degree-one element has volume 0, so a degree-one element cannot reach a hyperbolic closure through any of its words. A hyperbolic closure needs a word with at least two crossings (in fact at least four, since every link with crossing number at most 3 is non-hyperbolic).

Relation to higher-degree contributions. When the photon couples to a massive state \beta_m, the product \gamma \cdot \beta_m shifts in the degree-lex filtration by +1 but otherwise transforms representation content through the Pieri rule (Pieri photon shift). The lemma here is the base case of that ladder.
rem:phi-q-tower-jsj-bridge:
Remark Φ_q tower equals \rho_q \cdot \sum_S \mathrm{Vol}(K_S) (archimedean bridge).

Superseded. The scalar aether density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower).

Conjecture (\Phi_q-JSJ archimedean bridge). Under the archimedean realization, each summand of the dilogarithm tower evaluates precisely to the hyperbolic volume of the corresponding \Phi_q-piece, weighted by the aether density:

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl(z^{\lvert S\rvert} \cdot \Phi_q(\|V_S\|_F)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \rho_q \cdot
  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(S^3 \setminus K_S).

Summing over all subsets reconstructs the continuous JSJ piecewise sum.

This conjecture aligns the algebraic discrete evaluation with the geometric continuous evaluation. The dilogarithm pipeline and the hyperbolic-volume pipeline compute the identical archimedean target through different convergence regimes. It formalizes the quantum Bloch group regulator mapping the algebraic strata directly onto the JSJ decomposition.
prf:phi-q-tower-algebraic-stratification:
Proof Proof of phi q tower algebraic stratification.

  1. Algebraic stratification exists. For each S, \beta_S is a well-defined element of the braid group B_n (skein-smoothing commutes with the braid-group structure). Implication for the Newton–Raphson solver

The conjecture has a direct computational consequence: the zeros \{q_0^{-k}\} of the algebraic denominator are the exact initial seed values for the Newton–Raphson solver of the Thurston gluing equations on the active JSJ piece. The pipeline is:

  1. The algebraic engine computes \Phi_n(x; q_0) as a rational function.
  2. Extract the n roots of its denominator (x; q_0)_n: \{q_0^{-k} : k = 0, \dots, n-1\}.

  4. Use the roots not as a universal constant but as the initial guesses for the Newton–Raphson solver.

Discussion

Stated conditional on (algebraic-geometric dilog equivalence) and (Archimedean limit). The shared-denominator statement is a conditional result over a hypothesis that is not known to hold: the conjecture is open.

What keeps the hypothesis from being satisfiable by fiat is that the cusp shape assignment k \mapsto z_k is one of its parameters. Requiring a geometric shape, \mathrm{Im}\, z > 0, excludes real constants such as the "skeleton" z = 2 of an earlier revision, but a clause asserting only that some geometric shape exists is discharged by z = i for every q, x and n, since that existential is unlinked to the root index. Binding the shape as a parameter is what makes the conjecture constrain the cusp data supplied to it.

The conjecture then yields one consequence directly: at a root index the matched shape has \mathrm{Im}\, z_k > 0, so z_k is not real and in particular is not the bare algebraic seed q_0^{-k}. The SnapPy witness below reaches the same conclusion by measurement.

Empirical scope of the seeding pipeline

Two computational witnesses bracket the conjecture's strong form:

  • Color-tube cubic (succeeds): q-pochhammer-seed.witness.json drives Newton–Raphson on \Delta(z) = 0 from the algebraic seeds q_0^{-k} + 0.1i.   • SnapPy Thurston gluing system (bounds the strong form): snappy-cusp-seeding.witness.json measures the distance between the bare algebraic seeds and SnapPy's tetrahedral shape parameters for \mathtt{m004}, \mathtt{m003}, and the Borromean rings \mathtt{L6a4}. The bare seeds sit at distance \approx 0.4–0.9 from the recorded z_k, so the pole-to-shape correspondence is not the literal identity q_0^{-k} = z_k. Each seed is paired against the tetrahedral shape parameters, so what is measured is indexed by tetrahedron, not by cusp.

The two witnesses together support the conjecture's structural content (algebraic poles label the ideal tetrahedra) while bounding its canonical form (the bare q_0^{-k} are not literally the shape parameters).

No function of the seed can carry the index

The identity q_0^{-k} = z_k is excluded twice over, and neither exclusion needs the distances above.

It is already a (conditional) theorem. Conditional on the hypothesis above, z_k \neq r for every real r, because the requirement \mathrm{Im}\, z_k > 0 excludes every real shape and the seeds q_0^{-k} are real. So the identity fails for a reason internal to the conjecture.

The stronger statement is that the shapes do not separate the indices at all. An ideal tetrahedron carries three shape parameters — the relabelling orbit z \mapsto 1/(1-z) \mapsto 1 - 1/z, which leaves the tetrahedron unchanged — so two distinct recorded values may be one tetrahedron. Reading the committed witness through that orbit:

The roots are pairwise distinct since q_0 \neq 1. So on each of these triangulations an assignment seed value \mapsto shape is constant up to isometry, and a constant map cannot recover k.

This excludes every candidate function of the seed value — injective or not — on the three triangulations the corpus probes. It is a counting argument, and its invariant is the pigeonhole principle on a finite set; it does not exclude the conjecture.

What the conjecture asserts is not the shape. Its displayed right-hand side is the pair of holonomies \mathrm{Hol}_{\mu_k}, \mathrm{Hol}_{\lambda_k}, each a product of shape parameters along a meridian or longitude path. A holonomy is path-dependent, hence index-dependent even where the shapes are all equal — exactly the property the shapes lack. The quantity that tests the conjecture is therefore the gluing residual \lvert \mathrm{Hol}_{\mu_k} - 1 \rvert evaluated at the algebraic seeds, which neither witness computes.

Two indexings remain in tension and the resolution is open. The left side has n roots with n the partial-product order; the right side is indexed by cusps, and the two counts differ on every manifold probed above (2 against 1, 2 against 1, 8 against 3). A companion cardinality argument reaches the same conclusion from the ideal vertices of a single tetrahedron. Substituting "tetrahedron" for "cusp" is not available as a repair, since a holonomy is cusp data; for an ideal triangulation of a cusped manifold the tetrahedron-indexed gluing data is the edge equation, with one edge per tetrahedron, and the cusp-completeness conditions are the complementary set. Which of these the conjecture intends is not settled here.

Because the Borromean rings complement M_{\mathcal{B}_3} = \mathbf{S}^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3 is a complete finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold, the extended Bloch-group theorem of Walter D. The K-theoretic structure

The Bloch group B(F) of a field F is generated by symbols [z] for z \in F \setminus \{0, 1\} modulo the 5-term relation

  [x] + [y] + [1 - xy] + \bigl[\tfrac{1 - x}{1 - xy}\bigr] + \bigl[\tfrac{1 - y}{1 - xy}\bigr]
  \;=\;
  0,

which IS the Bloch-Wigner / Rogers Pentagon identity for the dilogarithm [kirillov1995, §1.1.4, §2.3.1]. Bloch–Suslin showed B(\mathbb{C}) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong K_3^{\text{ind}}(\mathbb{C}) \otimes \mathbb{Q}. Walter D. Neumann [neumann2004, §1, §14] lifts the Bloch–Wigner map to an isomorphism \lambda : H_3(\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})^\delta; \mathbb{Z}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) onto the extended Bloch group, proves that the Rogers-dilogarithm homomorphism R : \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{C}/\pi^2\mathbb{Z} satisfies (R \circ \lambda)([M]) = i\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}(M) + i\,\mathrm{CS}(M)\bigr) as the universal Cheeger–Chern–Simons class, and constructs the fundamental class [M] \in H_3(\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})^\delta; \mathbb{Z}) for every complete finite-volume non-compact hyperbolic 3-manifold (§14; surveyed in [arxiv-2304.12545v1, §3]).

The Beilinson regulator r_2: B(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R} is given by the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm:

  r_2([z]) \;=\; D(z)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \log|z| \cdot \arg(1 - z).

For an ideal tetrahedron with cross-ratio z = e^{i\theta} on the unit circle, \log|z| = 0, so the regulator collapses to the Clausen function

  D(e^{i\theta}) \;=\; \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}) \;=\; \mathrm{Cl}_2(\theta),
  \qquad
  \Lambda(\theta) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{Cl}_2(2\theta),

where \Lambda is the Lobachevsky function. So hyperbolic volume IS a regulator evaluation, per \mathrm{Vol}(K) as a motivic period: the Bloch--Wigner regulator reading of \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}. The two normalisations differ by both an argument doubling and a factor 2; keeping one function's coefficient while writing the other's name is a recurring slip.

The Borromean Bloch-group element

Per Quantum Bloch group and the pentagon identity and the classical Bloch-Suslin construction:

  • The Borromean complement decomposes into two regular ideal octahedra (Thurston), each of volume 4G = 4\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/2) \approx 3.66386.
  • In the Bloch group each octahedron is 4 \cdot [i], so the cross-ratio carried by the class is the fourth root of unity \zeta_4 = i = e^{i\pi/2} — not the sixth root e^{i\pi/3}, which is the figure-eight parameter.
  • The total Bloch-group element is
  [\mathcal{B}_3]_{B(\mathbb{C})}
  \;=\;
  8 \cdot [i]
  \;\in\;
  B(\mathbb{C}),

with regulator r_2[\mathcal{B}_3] = 8 \cdot D(i) = 8\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/2) = 8G (Catalan's constant; see Binding energy scale \alpha = m_e \times 8G). This is the \zeta_4 row of the transcendental-accounting table; the figure-eight sits in the \zeta_6 row with \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3).

The conjectural content — h^4 as the next-order regulator term

The Beilinson regulator extends to higher orders via the formal q-expansion of \Phi_q around q = 1 (the archimedean limit per (1{-}q)\,\log\Phi_n(x; q) \to \mathrm{Li}_2(x) under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}):

  \log \Phi_q(z)
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{q - 1}
  \bigl(
    \mathrm{Li}_2(z) + h \cdot R_1(z) + h^2 \cdot R_2(z) + \cdots
  \bigr),

where R_k(z) are higher-Bloch regulators. The conjecture is:

  \frac{r_2^{(2)}[\mathcal{B}_3]}{r_2[\mathcal{B}_3]}
  \;=\;
  h^4 \text{ coefficient of } \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_3, q)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{3}{4},

where r_2^{(2)} is the order-h^2 correction to the leading r_2 regulator. Equivalently: r_2^{(2)}[\mathcal{B}_3] = -6G.

Significance

Four candidate routes are open for deriving h^4 = -3/4 categorically:

  1. Direct Borromean Markov trace — already done
  2. Pachner-Pentagon state-sum — Pachner 2–3 move = Pentagon identity at Borromean ideal-tetrahedron decomposition
  3. K-theoretic / Bloch group regulator (this conjecture)
  4. DIM-master Pentagon — research-grade

Closing this conjecture ties h^4 to the K-theoretic structure of K_3(\mathbb{C}) — the deepest connection to motivic / arithmetic structure. It also closes the loop:

  • r_2 at order h^0 = 8G (the bare hyperbolic volume = production \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) in the canonical formalism),
